_comment: Design-system provenance for Cascadia Finance. Per the C-track provenance
Records which version of the shared standard governed this module's charts,
which theme build it actually ships, and how that was reviewed. The
theme_sha256 is what a drift check compares against the tag the module claims.
_origin_note: The honest answer, and it is recorded as a gap rather than smoothed over.
This module's nineteen charts across five pages shipped before the design
system carried chart obligations, and had never had a chart review — Rule
7.1 had been INVARIANT since v2.0. 'pre-standard' describes where the
charts came from; the adoption block below describes when that stopped

adopted.subject: Adopt the Cascadia signature in the shared layer

closed_by.subject: Close the fix round: 20 defects repaired, verdict SHIP

_theme_note: Verified byte-identical to the standards copy on 2026-08-25. No drift.
_panel_note: Four seats, spawned in parallel, no seat saw another's return. Widths given
to every seat were 1280 px (design) and 320 px (narrowest supported) —
which is what v2.5's materials condition on Rule 7.4 requires. The panel
raised 22 defects against a DO NOT SHIP verdict; the fix round repaired 20

retrospective_declaration.subject: Adopt the retroactivity convention as v2.6, and declare v2.1 through v2.5
retrospective_declaration.trigger: the module converts the next time its charts are regenerated by its build
retrospective_declaration.expiry: the next full-portfolio republish, after which this branch becomes retroactive
_note: governance/freeze.toml carried a promissory note against exactly this:
'Open item 20 is not yet adopted, so this proceeds under a retroactive
declaration: when item 20 lands, its retrospective v2.1-v2.5 declaration
must name this reskin and state its branch.' v2.6's declaration names
the 2026-08-12 reskin and states its branch. The note is discharged.
freeze.toml's own authorization history is left exactly as written —
the discharge is recorded here, not by editing that history.

known_nonconformance.summary: ECharts is loaded from the jsDelivr CDN on four published pages
known_nonconformance.conflicts_with: this repo's own CLAUDE.md, which forbids a CDN dependency for a chart library
known_nonconformance.blocked_on: all four pages are protected in governance/freeze.toml; vendoring is a frozen-page edit and needs its own authorization
